0de6b738938adf22450d13bcc1dd4310afc97e63.content:
{
  "Clean Code": "Source code that is easy to read, understand, and maintain, adhering to established best practices and design principles. It emphasizes clarity, simplicity, and structural integrity over clever or compact implementations.",
  "Readable Code": "Code written in a style that allows developers to easily comprehend its intent and logic without excessive effort. Readability is achieved through consistent formatting, meaningful naming, and logical organization.",
  "Maintainable Code": "Code structured in a way that facilitates future modification, extension, and debugging with minimal risk of introducing errors. It is characterized by modularity, clear abstractions, and low coupling between components.",
  "Function": "A named, reusable block of code that performs a specific task and may accept inputs and return outputs. In clean code practice, functions should be small, focused, and dedicated to a single responsibility.",
  "Single Responsibility": "A design property indicating that a code unit, such as a function or class, has exactly one reason to change and performs one well-defined task. It promotes cohesion and simplifies reasoning about code behavior.",
  "Class": "A programming construct that encapsulates related data (state) and behavior (methods) into a single cohesive unit. Classes serve as blueprints for creating objects and should adhere to the Single Responsibility Principle.",
  "Single Responsibility Principle": "A SOLID design principle stating that a class should have only one reason to change, meaning it should be responsible for a single piece of functionality. It helps reduce complexity and improve maintainability.",
  "Meaningful Name": "An identifier for a variable, function, class, or other code element that clearly conveys its purpose, intent, or usage. Meaningful names avoid random characters and abbreviations, favoring descriptive and self-explanatory wording.",
  "Code Comprehension": "The cognitive process by which a developer reads and understands the structure, behavior, and intent of source code. It is facilitated by clean code practices such as meaningful naming and clear organization.",
  "Comment": "An annotation embedded in source code that is ignored by the compiler or interpreter and intended for human readers. Effective comments explain the reasoning or rationale behind code decisions rather than restating what the code does.",
  "Method": "A function defined within a class that operates on instances of that class and implements part of its behavior. Methods provide the interface through which objects interact with their internal state and with other objects.",
  "Class Behavior": "The set of operations and actions a class can perform, typically defined and implemented through its methods. It represents the dynamic aspect of a class, in contrast to the static data it holds.",
  "Variable": "A named storage location in a program that holds a value which can change during execution. Variables represent the state of a program or object at a given point in time.",
  "State": "The current values of all variables and data held by a program, object, or system at a specific moment. State determines the behavior and output of code when operations are performed.",
  "Abbreviation": "A shortened form of a word or phrase used in place of its full version, often to save space. In clean code, abbreviations are generally discouraged in identifiers because they reduce clarity and hinder comprehension."
}
